key_insight: Bayesian inference combined with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize perovskite solar cell degradation to specific interfaces or the bulk over time.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a practical way to diagnose failure mechanisms spatially and target stability improvements such as interface passivation.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated devices
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to experimental observations
Bayesian inference to infer spatial maps of recombination-related parameters
evidence_signal: The study tracks inferred parameter maps during aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and finds pronounced non-uniform degradation, strongest near perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The inferred degradation maps depend on model assumptions and imaging quality, so incorrect physics or sparse data could bias the localization of failure.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
